Footage from the lab and the field, mostly high-speed and slowed way down. Scroll through, or jump to a full writeup: [Do tadpoles even have lungs?](research/do-tadpoles-have-lungs.qmd), [Why lose a lung?](research/why-lose-a-lung.qmd), and [Bubble guts](research/bubble-guts.qmd).

::: {.video-figure}
{{< video assets/video/schismaderma-breathing-sequence.mp4 >}}

**A whole school of tadpoles surfacing for air at once, then sinking back down**
Filmed with a 600mm lens at a roadside pond in Limpopo, South Africa. Each school is roughly the size of a beach ball. More in [Bubble guts](research/bubble-guts.qmd).
:::

::: {.video-figure}
{{< video assets/video/rana-clamitans-breach-bounce.mp4 >}}

**A small green frog tadpole (*Rana clamitans*) tries to breach**
It swims up mouth-first, but the surface doesn't break. It stretches under the impact and springs back, sending the tadpole down without a breath. From [Do tadpoles even have lungs?](research/do-tadpoles-have-lungs.qmd)
:::

::: {.video-figure}
{{< video assets/video/rana-clamitans-bubble-suck.mp4 >}}

**An older, much larger *Rana clamitans* tadpole successfully breaches**
Breaching is closer to what whales do: coming up quickly through the surface and exchanging air while briefly above it. From [Do tadpoles even have lungs?](research/do-tadpoles-have-lungs.qmd)
:::

::: {.video-figure}
{{< video assets/video/xenopus-laevis-bubble-suck.mp4 >}}

**A young tadpole bubble sucking**
Instead of breaking through the surface, the tadpole presses its mouth to the underside and sucks a pocket of the air-water interface down into its mouth. From [Do tadpoles even have lungs?](research/do-tadpoles-have-lungs.qmd)
:::

::: {.video-figure}
{{< video assets/video/rana-sylvatica-bubble-suck.mp4 >}}

**Bubble sucking, a second view**
The same behavior from a different angle: mouth pressed to the surface, bubble pulled downward, then pinched off and swallowed. From [Do tadpoles even have lungs?](research/do-tadpoles-have-lungs.qmd)
:::

::: {.video-figure}
{{< video assets/video/xenopus-laevis-bubble-suck-detail.mp4 >}}

**Bubble sucking, up close**
Watch closely and you can see each phase of the breath, including the lungs emptying mid-suck and refilling afterward. From [Do tadpoles even have lungs?](research/do-tadpoles-have-lungs.qmd)
:::

::: {.video-figure}
{{< video assets/video/pond-snail-under-surface-film.mp4 >}}

**A pond snail walking along the underside of the surface**
The same surface tension that lets water striders stand on top of the water acts as a ceiling from below, and this snail is using it as a walking surface. From [Do tadpoles even have lungs?](research/do-tadpoles-have-lungs.qmd)
:::

::: {.video-figure}
{{< video assets/video/snail-bubble-suck.mp4 >}}

**A pond snail (*Physa heterostrophus*) bubble-sucking**
No mouth involved this time: the pulmonary siphon does the same job, pulling the surface down and sealing off a bubble before drawing it in. From [Do tadpoles even have lungs?](research/do-tadpoles-have-lungs.qmd)
:::

::: {.video-figure}
{{< video assets/video/spea-intermontana-breath-comparison.mp4 >}}

**An ordinary air breath, from a tadpole with ordinary lungs**
*Spea intermontana*, filmed for comparison against the lungless breathing in [Bubble guts](research/bubble-guts.qmd) and [Why lose a lung?](research/why-lose-a-lung.qmd). Mouth open, straight up through the surface, gulp, done.
:::
